knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.2.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. For an IID Normal sample, which statement correctly describes confidence intervals for the mean and for the variance?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the statement that covers both Normal mean and variance CIs.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Normal mean and Normal variance intervals use different pivots (t/z versus chi-square). One does not stand in for the other, and binomial recipes are a different setting.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Mean CI via Normal/t pivot; variance CI via chi-square pivot on s².
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating the mean CI as enough, or reusing the mean formula for σ².

choices.label: A CI for the mean typically uses a Normal or t pivotal structure (as appropriate when σ is known or unknown). A CI for the variance typically uses a chi-square structure based on the sample variance.
A CI for the mean finishes the requirement; the variance interval uses the same t formula with s² in place of s.
Both the mean and the variance use the same binomial Normal approximation interval because Normal data are approximately binomial for large n.
A CI for σ² is formed as x̄ ± z s/√n, the same centre as the mean interval.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.2.4
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. IID Normal sample, n=16, x̄=10, s²=4 (σ unknown). Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Both mean and variance CI forms; refuse mean-only / binomial conflation.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: With σ unknown, the mean CI uses t_{n−1}. The variance CI inverts the chi-square pivot for (n−1)s²/σ². Mean-only or Normal-SE-for-variance shortcuts fail the dual requirement.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: t interval for μ; chi-square interval for σ²; both required.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Using z with unknown σ, skipping the variance CI, or forcing a Normal-mean SE onto σ².

choices.label: For μ use x̄ ± t_{15, 1−α/2} · s/√n. For σ² use ((n−1)s² / χ²_{15, 1−α/2}, (n−1)s² / χ²_{15, α/2}). Both forms are required; a binomial interval is a different setting.
For μ use x̄ ± z_{1−α/2} · s/√n with z even though σ is unknown; the variance CI can be skipped once the mean CI is written.
For μ use x̄ ± t_{15, 1−α/2} · s/√n, and for σ² reuse that same numerical interval because variance intervals share the mean endpoints.
For σ² use (s² − z s/√n, s² + z s/√n), centred at s² with Normal mean SE.
